ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and UBOs against the OFAC SDN List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions imposed under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and the RCMP/Canadian sanctions list; mandatory enhanced Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) due diligence under the PCMLTFA Regulations and FINTRAC guidance; automated re-screening at least every 90 days and immediately upon material changes; all results must be minuted and retained for not less than five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec – Services en ligne / Registre des entreprises (REQ) at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must comply with the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, ss. 302 et seq. The name must be in French unless it is an official-filing recognized trade-mark, an established name in a recognized minority context, or an English-only name accompanied by a French corporate version. The legal ending must be 'Inc.' (or 'Corp.'/'Ltee' where permitted), and the declaration of name reservation must use the Latin alphabet with no accents required for type of corporation but accents mandatory for proper French spelling. No transliteration to a non-Latin script is accepted by the REQ.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When the Registraire des entreprises refuses a proposed name, the applicant must file a written request for reconsideration with the REQ within 30 days of the refusal, stating the legal grounds and annexing a new NUANS-style name search report; alternatively the applicant may immediately submit one or more new names for reservation. If the refusal concerns a sensitive token, the applicant may apply directly to the relevant competent ministry for prior written approval before resubmitting. Judicial review is available in the Superior Court of Quebec if the administrative remedy is exhausted. No formal extension of the 90-day name reservation is permitted; re-filing and re-payment of the statutory fee is required for a further 90-day period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partial. A virtual office / business address in Quebec is acceptable solely as the statutory registered office address, provided it is a real street address located in Quebec and corporate records are accessible or service of process can be accepted at that address. A virtual address cannot be used as the licensed premises for craft beer distribution, warehousing, or cold-chain keg storage, and will not satisfy the requirements of the Act respecting the Societe des alcools du Quebec (CQLR c S-5) or the Regie des alcools, des courses et des jeux licensing regime. A physical, zoning-compliant commercial premises is mandatory for operational substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (approximately 65% likelihood within the first 12 months) due to mandatory RACJ/SAQ permit inspections, municipal commercial zoning audits, and targeted FINTRAC compliance examinations for licensed alcoholic beverage distributors; unannounced on-site inspections are expressly permitted under the relevant provincial and municipal statutes.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed under the Enterprise Registration Act, CQLR c R-5
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for consideration fixed by the board. No escrow account requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation subscribes to the shares listed within the share subscription agreement, and the Board determines consideration therefor in accordance with the Business Corporations Act (Quebec). RESOLVED, that the registered office for the Corporation be established at Montreal, Quebec, and that notice thereof be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Name Search (CIDREQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-incorporation name search in the Registraire’s database to ensure distinctiveness. Submit a name reservation request through the online portal, using the proposed corporate name and Canadian legal element (e.g., 'Brewcorp Ignore Inc.').
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name request is queried, file a revised declaration with a new proposed name or submit a request for authorization to use a borderline name within the objection period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or authorized online service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft articles of incorporation in the prescribed form, including variables such as share structure and class rights. Execute the articles through a notarized deed or authenticated electronic signature.
required_dossiers: Agency mandate or resolution authorizing signatories
Proof of registered office address (notarial attestation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any form deficiencies by preparing amending articles and re-submitting to the same notary or service provider for fresh execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (online portal: registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed articles and associated documents through the online filing system. Pay the prescribed filing fee and wait for issuance of the certificate of incorporation (attestation de constitution).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused, cure any compliance gaps, pay any outstanding fees, and file a new application; alternatively request administrative reconsideration from the Registraire.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Initial Corporate Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Incorporated Entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to approve share subscriptions, formally adopt by-laws, appoint the initial officers, and ratify the registered office address. Record minutes of the meeting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resolution is found defective, the board may void and re-adopt it via unanimous shareholder resolution under the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Registry Declaration and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of incorporation, file the initial declaration with the Registraire. Register for GST/QST accounts, employee payroll accounts, and any import/export accounts through Revenu Québec’s CLIC portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing penalties may be withdrawn through an application for voluntary disclosure, provided the omission was inadvertent and corrective action is initiated before assessment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Effluent quality criteria: BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, TSS ≤ 30 mg/L, pH 6.0–8.5; VOC controls per the Clean Air Act (CQLR c E-6.1); spent grain and packaging waste management under Extended Producer Responsibility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA/ARC) — federal corporate income tax, federal excise duty regime, and GST/HST policy; Revenu Québec (RQ) — Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec corporate income tax, and day-to-day GST/HST administration in Quebec pursuant to a collection agreement with CRA. Portals: CRA My Business Account (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); RQ Clic SÉQUOIA / Mon dossier d'entreprise (www.revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act (federal) or Quebec Business Corporations Act; Quebec incorporation or extra-provincial registration is effected through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, which issues the 10-digit NEQ (Quebec enterprise number). 2. Federal incorporations are automatically seeded with a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN/NE) by CRA; provincial incorporations must register for the BN via CRA's 'Newly Incorporated Business' online service. 3. File Revenu Québec Form LM-1 or register online to obtain the GST/HST program account (BN + 'RT' suffix) and the QST registration number (NEQ-based, 'TQ' suffix); in Quebec, GST/HST registration is processed by Revenu Québec. 4. If the corporation will hold duty-unpaid excise goods (e.g., bonded keg inventory), obtain an excise warehouse licence under the Excise Act, 2001 via CRA; a pure wholesaler distributing duty-paid beer does not require an excise licence. 5. Register with Revenu Québec for provincial corporate income tax (Form CO-1027). 6. Foreign-incorporated entities carrying on business in Quebec must also obtain an NEQ and register for GST/QST before invoicing Quebec customers; non-resident shareholders are permitted without restriction on Canadian residency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box pass-through election exists under Canadian law. The Business Corporation is taxed at entity level on worldwide income (federal Part I tax plus Quebec corporate tax), with 'Canadian-controlled private corporation' status potentially qualifying for the federal small business deduction (9% on active business income up to CAD 500,000) and the Quebec reduced rate (3.2% on the same base). Available statutory elections include: (i) GST/HST closely-related corporation joint election (Excise Tax Act s. 156 and QST Act equivalent) treating qualifying related registrants as one registrant; (ii) GST/HST joint venture election (ETA s. 273 / QST equivalent); (iii) Income Tax Act s. 85 rollover election on asset transfers to the corporation; (iv) no elective opt-out for the hybrid mismatch rules — mandated deduction-denial provisions under ITA ss. 12.6–12.93 and related provisions apply automatically to cross-border hybrid arrangements after June 30, 2022.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax under the Excise Tax Act) combined with QST (Quebec Sales Tax under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax); dual value-added tax applied at federal and provincial levels.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small-supplier registration threshold measured by worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated exports) over any four consecutive calendar quarters; applies equally to GST/HST and QST. Export-oriented wholesalers typically register voluntarily even below the threshold to recover input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or mandatory digital stamping regime exists in Canada. E-invoicing is voluntary, with PEPPOL BIS 3.0 / UBL adoption promoted through Canada's 'Business Connect' initiative. Statutory invoice content is prescribed (supplier and recipient identity, GST/HST and QST registration numbers, dates, tax rates and amounts — ETA s. 3 and QST Act equivalents). In Quebec, the Charter of the French Language requires French to be used in commercial documents such as catalogues and contracts; business records must be kept in Canada and made available to CRA and Revenu Québec inspectors, in French or English, upon demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods, including craft beer and kegs, qualify for a 0% GST/HST and 0% QST rate where the supply is made in Canada and the goods are transferred to a non-resident recipient or a common carrier for export promptly after sale, per ETA Schedule VI s. 23 and corresponding QST Act provisions. The goods must not be consumed in Canada. Offshore services (e.g., international distribution or logistics consultancy supplied to a non-resident) qualify for zero-rating under ETA Schedule VI s. 7 where the services are performed outside Canada or relate to foreign property. For excise duty paid on beer produced in Canada and later exported, a drawback/rebate is claimable under s. 124 of the Excise Act, 2001 within two years of the duty payment; Quebec's specific tax on alcoholic beverages does not attach to exported product.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Form B13A (Goods to Be Exported) or electronic export declaration filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED) for non-U.S. destinations; U.S.-bound shipments are ordinarily exempt from B13A unless controlled or permitted goods are involved
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment from Canada to the non-resident consignee
Commercial invoice reconciling to the B13A/CAED filing, with HS code 2203.00 for malt beer
Proof-of-export evidential package retained per CRA GST/HST Memorandum 4.5 (carrier certificates, customs stamps, container tracking movements, port storage records)

Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT wire advice, or bank statement demonstrating receipt of foreign currency from the non-resident buyer — a CRA audit documentation benchmark rather than a statutory requirement
Excise Act, 2001 drawback application (with supporting production and export records) where excise duty was paid on the exported beer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating where export evidence is incomplete, contradictory, or the goods return to Canada. The denied exporter must remit the full combined rate of 14.975% (5% GST + 9.975% QST) on the sale value, plus prescribed-rate interest and penalties. Gross-negligence false-statement penalties apply: ETA s. 285 imposes the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the tax sought to be evaded; the Quebec Tax Administration Act mirrors this for QST. The ordinary four-year reassessment window is suspended indefinitely where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established. Criminal tax evasion (ETA s. 327 and equivalent Quebec provisions) carries fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to five years. Export pricing to related non-resident distributors is also scrutinized under OECD-aligned transfer-pricing rules, with CRA's Aggressive Tax Planning unit able to adjust values, deny deductions, and apply transfer-pricing penalties of 10% of the net adjustment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary and Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) licensing authority; OSFI supervises federally chartered banks; FINTRAC enforces cross-border electronic funds transfer (EFT) reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada maintains no separate foreign-exchange administration; the Minister of Finance retains dormant discretionary exchange-control powers under the Currency Act and Foreign Exchange Regulations, which are not invoked for ordinary trade.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CAD is fully convertible under IMF Article VIII for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no FX approval, quantitative ceiling, or waiting period for profit remittance, dividend repatriation, or capital outflow. The only statutory frictions are Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) solvency gating for distributions and Part XIII withholding tax (25% statutory; reduced to 5%/15% under the Canada-US treaty) on dividends. Non-resident ownership is unrestricted, dividends may be declared in USD or CAD, and no currency-export permit is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no forced conversion ratio; exporters retain 100% of USD and other foreign-currency receipts in multicurrency accounts. The applicable statutory obligations are: (i) CBSA B13A export declaration for shipments above C$2,000 or controlled goods; (ii) FINTRAC EFT report for every international electronic transfer equal to or greater than C$10,000; (iii) Statistics Canada balance-of-payments (BOP) threshold-reporting for international transactions; and (iv) federal-beneficial-ownership registry filings (Bill C-42) for the reporting entity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account: multi-currency CAD/USD treasury package with dedicated FX dealing desk and U.S. subsidiary clearing
Capital Escrow Account: Quebec-headquartered cooperative bank preferred for QBCA closing accounts and share-subscription escrow
Operational Account: RBC Express International wire platform plus cross-border USD sweep to RBC U.S. branch
Operational Account: USD concentration account with BMO Harris Bank corridor for USD-payables clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability. Foreign digital EMIs (Wise Platform, Airwallex, Corpay, OFX, Payoneer) may operate only as FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses (MSBs) and must partner with an approved Payments Canada clearing agent to settle CAD. Bank of Canada RPAA licensing applies from 2024-2025, adding a dual-federal regulatory layer. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot grant deposit insurance, cannot issue Canadian deposit accounts, cannot provide overdraft/credit, and cannot issue standby letters of credit; they are therefore unacceptable for escrowed share capital, LC-backed equipment imports, or primary treasury concentration. Recommended narrow use: sub-C$10,000 operational disbursements to overseas hops/glassware suppliers and fast USD-to-CAD conversions for small invoices only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted under FINTRAC identity-verification methods (dual-process or technology-based verification), but Quebec-tier banks and Desjardins nevertheless require: (i) notarized proof-of-identity and proof-of-address for every director and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO); (ii) an in-branch signature or Quebec-remote notarial 'pink-slip' attestation for permanent account-for-export forms; and (iii) a live video interview with the UBO when no director is Canadian resident. Practical mandate: at least one Canadian-resident director, preferably Metro-Montreal based, must attend one physical branch session at National Bank or Desjardins; this reduces onboarding from 6-8 weeks (fully remote) to 2-4 weeks and materially improves the entity's AML risk score.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO injecting initial equity in USD from a personal offshore brokerage or bank account without audited source-of-funds trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share-subscription agreement; director and UBO 24-month source-of-wealth bank statements; Quebec Registraire des entreprises excerpt; CBCA/QBCA certificate of incorporation; CRA tax clearance and nil-offset letter; US distributor contract as corroborating business purpose; negative media/sanctions screening report (World-Check or equivalent); beneficial-ownership registry filing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Triangular payment patterns where US state wholesalers or provincial liquor boards pay amounts differing from commercial invoice values to a second entity in the corporate group.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execution-ready distribution agreements with SAQ or RACJ-licensed counterparties; itemized commercial invoices with PO cross-reference; proof-of-delivery / CMR or BOL; CBSA B13A export declarations; FINTRAC EFT report copies; intercompany transfer-pricing documentation under OECD Chapter IV; consolidated A/R aging ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent USD-to-CAD conversions without a documented hedging policy, setting off the bank's FX desk and complex-transaction surveillance reviews.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury and FX policy naming National Bank/RBC as sole dealing counterparty; ISDA 2002 or bank master FX terms; daily dealing tickets and forward confirmations; margin-call ledger; monthly cash-flow forecast and USD exposure report; inventory movement and cold-chain temperature-monitor logs for keg consignments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border sale into US states with strict alcohol-regulatory licensing, creating counterparty risk when US buyer appears as a shell storefront with cannabis adjacency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: TTB importer permit and state alcohol-beverage-control license verification for each US wholesale buyer; Dun & Bradstreet and Brewers Association screening; customer risk-assessment questionnaire; product-liability insurance certificate minimizing at C$10 million; explicit distribution-clause covenant isolating controlled substances from beer inventory; state age-verification compliance program.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (i) sender initiates SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to National Bank or Desjardins USD-clearing account; field 57A must state the Canadian bank's own SWIFT BIC, not an intermediate; (ii) field 70 (Remittance Information) must include 'CONTR SHARE CAP' or 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' together with the subscriber's corporate registration number, avoiding invoice or borrowing-language wording; (iii) if capital exceeds C$10,000, FINTRAC EFT report is mandatory; (iv) Bank of Canada BOP reporting captures the transaction under 'equity capital' purpose code; (v) for maximum traceability, route USD to the bank's U.S. clearing affiliate (e.g., NBC U.S., BMO Harris) and effect same-day LVTS transfer to the CAD operating account, executing conversion against a fixed dealing-desk quote of 0.25-0.75% above mid-market; (vi) file the share-subscription escrow release instruction with the bank's corporate-trust team to evidence the QBCA solvency condition.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for the Quebec microbrewery distributor: (i) U.S. raw-material purchases (malted barley, hops, cans): SWIFT MT103 from the USD operating account, or US ACH-IAT for transactions below US$50,000 to avoid wire fees; (ii) equipment and European glass imports: irrevocable commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700 with bills-of-lading presented through the bank's trade desk, costing approximately 1.5% p.a. on LC value plus documentary-collection fees; (iii) domestic C$ supplier payments under C$10,000: Payments Canada ACSS local direct debit / pre-authorized debit rails; (iv) large Canadian freight, brewery, or keg purchases: LVTS wire settlement; (v) standby export-contract support: MT760 standby LC issued to US distributors; (vi) all foreign disbursements must be recorded with CBSA export/import declarations where applicable and mirror the FX hedge position to avoid an unhedged bare USD short.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable vanilla FX forwards (USD/CAD and EUR/CAD) with tenors up to 24 months under simple bank master agreements
FX swaps combining spot sale and forward repurchase of USD/CAD for cash-flow smoothing
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for matched USD-receivable term funding
Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars on USD/CAD for earnings protection
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to non-deliverable crosses (e.g., CAD/BRL, CAD/ARS); not applicable to convertible USD/CAD
Bank-issued bid and performance guarantee bonds denominated in USD for cross-border supply contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Province of Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the corporation's Quebec registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the corporation to administrative monetary penalties; after a prolonged default, the REQ may publish a notice of possible administrative dissolution and strike the enterprise from the registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (where the entity is federally incorporated and registered extra-provincially in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A two-year failure to file may lead to administrative dissolution pursuant to section 212 of the CBCA; restoration requires filing arrears and paying late filing penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporate Income Tax Return and Quebec CO-17 Corporate Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of delay (maximum 12 months) applies; interest accrues on unpaid balances, and directors may face liability for unremitted source deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) - internal confirmation and maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained at the registered office; producible to REQ, Revenu Québec, and other enforcement authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the time of the annual general meeting; any change must be recorded within 15 days of the corporation becoming aware of it
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or make available the ISC register is an offence under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and, for CBCA corporations, under the CBCA, attracting substantial fines and possible director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, a non-reporting issuer has no automatic financial-size audit threshold; the shareholders may unanimously waive auditor appointment. Mandatory independent audit is triggered if the corporation is a reporting issuer, if the articles or a unanimous shareholder agreement so require, or if shareholders holding a sufficient interest statutorily requisition an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable or reporting enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) for private Quebec corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec law requires every QBCA corporation to maintain an internal register of individuals with significant control and to update it when controlling interests change; no separate public UBO annual filing is currently made to the REQ. The annual declaration to REQ captures current directors and officers. Secretarial protocol requires the ISC register to be reconciled against the register of members and transfer records at each annual general meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 8,500 for a small private craft-brewery distribution entity if an independent audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.5% (federal 13% net of provincial abatement + Quebec general rate 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 14% combined small business deduction on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (federal 9% + Quebec 5%); additional provincial investment tax credits, innovation credits, accelerated capital cost allowance, and SR&ED tax credit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; NETFILE via CRA-certified tax software or CRA My Business Account (mandatory e-file for corporations with gross revenue exceeding CAD 1 million).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; fiscal period elected in T2 cannot exceed 12 months without special permission.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than six months after the fiscal period end; instalments due quarterly on the last day of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, registered office, fiscal period start and end dates, jurisdiction of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations report Canadian business income and must indicate Canada-Quebec permanent establishment accordingly; treaty-based non-residents may claim exemption with supporting schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue: keg sales, distribution commissions, transportation charges, and other wholesale income from ISIC 4632 operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source business revenue allocable to the Quebec permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 300/316 (Taxable Income and Part I Tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute federal taxable income after non-capital loss carryforward, foreign tax credits, and national abatement; apply the Part I tax rate and small business deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents completing the non-resident share of taxable income may claim treaty deductions and must complete Schedule 91 (foreign tax credit) and Schedule 97 if a non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate Part I tax, federal surtax, and provincial tax allocation in respect of Quebec; reflects instalment payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a permanent establishment in Quebec report tax allocation under the Social Insurance Number (RC) or use schedule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeat failure penalty 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; arrears interest at prescribed rate compounded daily; prosecution for failure to file can result in fines.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return; Revenu Québec CLICKUS online portal; electronically filed by tax professionals or direct online with Revenu Québec.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due six months after the fiscal period end; quarterly instalments for estimated priorities exceeding CAD 1,500.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec business number (NEQ), registered address, fiscal period, legal nature of corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Quebec state their permanent establishment and agent details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and cost of sales from craft beer distribution; Quebec deduction for uncollectible accounts and inventory losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Residency status and allocation keys under the Quebec economic allocation formula for multi-province income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from active business, capital gains, dividends, and any recapture; applies Quebec non-capital loss deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only Quebec-source active business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec corporate rate and deductions (general rate, small business deduction, e-commerce tax credit, production of alcoholic beverages tax credit).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Schedule of tax credits for innovation or film may not apply; treaty withholding adjustment may affect the Quebec credit claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late CO-17 filing: 5% of the balance due plus 1% per month for a maximum of 12 months; a late-filing penalty of CAD 50 to CAD 1,000 for failure without tax payable; interest accrues daily; Revenu Québec administratively prosecutes tax evasion with fines of up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment under the Tax Administration Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII Canadian withholding tax on taxable dividends paid to non-residents; reduced to 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for substantial holdings under the Canada-U.S. treaty and equivalent DTA thresholds.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty-reduced rates, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide to the Canadian payer a completed Form NR301 (Declaration of Residency in Canada) or a foreign certificate of residence (e.g., IRS Form 6166); the payer applies the reduced withholding only if the certificate is current and the recipient is the beneficial owner; issuers that over-withhold may seek refund under CRA and Revenu Québec procedures within statutory limitation periods; a lack of certification results in statutory 25% withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 25% subject to domestic exemption for arm's-length interest on certain debt and treaty rates as low as 0-10%. Royalties: statutory 25% Part XIII; treaty rates commonly 0-10% (Canada-US: 0% for copyright on artistic works, 10% for know-how and service intangibles; Canada-UK: 10% on most royalties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 per non-arm's-length transaction series (goods/services); group Master File required where consolidated group revenue exceeds CAD 50,000,000; Local File must be contemporaneous and filed with the income tax return only upon CRA request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate the offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the manner of Caribbean/QFC jurisdictions; however, taxpayers must satisfy business-purpose and economic substance requirements through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245), Quebec's GAAR provision, and the capital equity test; a structure lacking actual management, employees, premises or economic risk may be disregarded or recharacterised.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating craft beer revenue, operating an unregistered parallel distribution cash system, manipulating inventory valuation, failing to remit Part XIII withholding on foreign dividend payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% to 200% of tax evaded under ITA and Quebec Taxation Act fines; prosecution may impose imprisonment of up to 5 years; interest and gross negligence penalties assessed on entire unreported income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for corporate withholding tax source deductions and GST/QST remittances (ITA s.227.1; Excise Tax Act s.323); where evasion is directed by an officer, that officer faces personal conviction, travel restrictions, issuance of an arrest warrant, and seizure of personal property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Quebec-incorporated entity without employees, premises, office, or inventory movement; routing transaction through that entity solely to claim treaty benefits or the provincial small business deduction; maintaining nominee directors with no decision-making role.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA and Revenu Québec realign the transaction under GAAR; denies treaty relief and reclassifies the income as personal income to owners; penalties equal to 50% of disallowed benefits may be imposed; in Quebec, a 'shelf company' misuse may trigger revocation of registrations and a sanction of CAD 5,000 to CAD 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced if the corporation is a sham; nominal directors (who accept fees and are not involved) are held personally liable for tax debts and may be named in consent orders prohibiting departure from Canada until the liability is discharged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging intercompany distribution fees below arm's length, failure to prepare or update the Canada/Quebec Local File, improperly categorising a revenue-sharing payment as royalty instead of profit distribution, lack of economic substance in the tested party's risk profile.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.247(3) penalties: 10% of the net adjustment (apply to the decline of revenues or profits shifted), minimum CAD 500, plus reassessed tax and interest; for repeat offenders, 20% of the adjustment; Quebec mirrors this in provincial tax law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may avoid TP penalty individually, but where they knowingly sign false certificates under the T2 or CO-17, they face disqualification from serving as directors for up to 7 years under the Canada Business Corporations Act; personal liability for unpaid amounts is not assessed unless fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately accepting and paying for craft beer distribution via unverified third-party digital wallets or shell bank accounts, failing to report large cash transactions exceeding CAD 10,000, or directing payments to embargoed jurisdictions without compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA): administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 per violation; criminal indictment for each offence imposes a fine of up to CAD 2,000,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for corporate AML fines if involved in laundering, and may be the subject of freezing orders, asset forfeiture, and travel bans; individuals who fail to supervise compliance may receive prison sentences up to 2 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, or management fees to related non-resident entities without applying 25% Part XIII tax or validating treaty claims; failure to file information returns NR4 Summary/Return and the T5 information slips.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unpaid Part XIII tax is recoverable with interest from the payer; penalties equal to 10% of the amount that should have been withheld if the payer failed to withhold (ITA s.227(9)); in Quebec, provincial penalties under the Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate directors become personally liable under a deemed trust for unremitted withholding taxes (salary, dividends, royalties, interest); the Canada Revenue Agency may register a security interest against personal assets and obtain an international travel ban under the Criminal Code if the amount is wilful.
